findings.title: Customer wants additional seats to extend program to seasonal crew (budget/purchasing matter)
findings.description: Curtis says he wishes he had more seats so he could open the coaching program to his seasonal crew, not just year-round staff. He explicitly frames this as a budget conversation he needs to have with his owner, not a BetterBark product problem. No product defect or missing capability is described; this is a licensing/seat-count/purchasing matter, and the account manager offered to help him build an internal business case rather than treating it as a product gap.
findings.quote: I wish I had more seats so I could open it to the seasonal crew too, not just the year-round staff
findings.severity_reason: Not a product defect or feature gap; explicitly a customer-side budget/purchasing consideration with no functional impact.
findings.match_note: Not in catalogue and not filed as a feature request; customer himself disclaims it as a product ask, calling it 'not a you problem'.

findings.title: Positive feedback on coach-to-customer matching quality (frontline-appropriate coach)
findings.description: Curtis reports his head dock master's assigned coach communicates well with frontline/blue-collar staff rather than using 'HR language,' which he credits as key to adoption. This is praise about coach-matching quality, not a complaint or defect, and Curtis asked that the feedback be passed along to the matching team rather than requesting any product change.
findings.quote: My dock master's coach in particular clearly gets the frontline world — doesn't talk to him in HR language, which would've killed it instantly.
findings.severity_reason: Purely positive, informational feedback with no defect or unmet need; no functional impact to assess.
findings.match_note: No corresponding catalogue issue; not a defect or feature request, just qualitative feedback to relay internally to the coach-matching team.
